full_judgment:
Mohammad Abdur Rouf, J: One Pran Gopal Kundu, resident of Chandpur was the owner of I he property in question situated in the District of Munshiganj. In vested property Case No. 113 of 1968 the disputed property was first declared as enemy property and subsequently as a vested property, on the ground that the said owner had left this country for India. But the said owner Pran Gopal Kundu filed objection Case No. 102 of 1995 before the Settlement Officer claiming ownership of the property and for correction of the records of right where his name was wrongly recorded as Indian national. The present petitioner as respondent No. 5 and lessee of the suit property of the government also filed objection Case No. 96 of 1975 disputing the claim of the said Pran Copal Kundu. Another person also filed another objection Case No. 59 of 1975 for recording the disputed property in his name. The Assistant Settlement Officer heard all those objection Cases on 17.6.76. Pran Copal Kundu appeared in person and conducted the case. By an order dated 5. 8. 76, the Assistant Settlement Officer allowed Objection Case No. 102 011975 and rejected the other two Objection Cases including that of the petitioner. IL was held that the owner Pran Gopal Kundu being a citizen of Bangladesh, the property was wrongly recorded as vested property. Thereafter respondent No. 1 by three registered kabalas dated 12. 2. 81, 19. 2. 81 and 20.2.81 purchased 4.12 acres of land in total including the disputed land from the said Pran Gopal Kundu and on 9. 3. 83 he prayed for releasing the land from the vested property list. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Munshiganj rejected his application on 30. 5. 86 refusing to release the land in question from the list of vested property. Upon an appeal preferred by respondent No. 1, the Additional Commissioner Dhaka Division of 12. 4. 87 allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) (Anx. C to the writ petition) and directed to release the property from the list of the vested property. The present petitioner on 30. 1. 89 filed revisional application against the said order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner. Dhaka before the Land Administration Board and the said Board affirmed the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner. On 7. 8. 90 the Secretary, Ministry of Land, (Respondent No. 2) how-ever, set aside the order of the Land Administration Board and restored that of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) (Anx. E to the writ petition). Against that order, respondent No. 1 filed a review application before respondent No. 2 who disposed of the same by an order dated 5.1.92 affirming his earlier order dated 7.8.90 rejecting the review application (Anx. F to the writ petition). Respondent No.1 then challenged the legality and propriety of those two orders dated 7.8.90 and 5.1.92 (Anx. E and F respectively of the writ petition) and obtained a Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 1093 of 1992. Present respondent Nos 2-5 jointly and the petitioner, added respondent No. 5 in the writ petition. contested the rule by filing two sets of affidavit-in-opposition supporting the impugned orders and denying the case of writ petitioner. 

 3. Mr. N. H. Khandaker, learned Advocate-on-Record of the petitioner submits that the petitioner in his affidavit-in-opposition asserted before the High Court Division that 4 khatians are involved in the case land and in two khatians Pran Gopal Kundu had only 1 annas 12 gandas share while in the other two khatians he had no share at all and that the alleged power of attorney dated 22.7.78, said to have been executed by said Pran Gopal (Aux. A to the writ petition) also does not include the case property and that the alleged 4 sale deeds of the year 1981 and 1982 (Anx. B series to the writ petition) said to have been executed by the so called attorney of the said Pran Gopal by virtue of the said power of Attorney in favour of the writ petitioner-respondent No. 1 were executed in contravention of President's Order Nos. 29 and 142 of 1972 and that in consideration of those facts, Respondent No. 2 set aside the order passed by the Land Administration Board vide Anx. E to the writ petition and maintained the same rejecting the review petition filed by respondent No. 1 vide Anx. F to the writ petition. But the learned Judges of the High Court erred in setting aside those orders without considering at all the facts mentioned above.
